subject: maths
title: Primary 4 Nets of Solids: Cubes, Cuboids, Prisms and Pyramids
seo_title: P4 Nets Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths on Solids and Nets with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Identifying and drawing 2D representations of cube, cuboid, cone, cylinder, prism and pyramid; identifying nets; identifying the solid formed by a net
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice on nets: name solids, count faces, edges and vertices, find nets of a cube and cuboid. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A net is a flat shape that folds into a solid: each part of the net becomes one face.
key_sub: 6 equal squares make a cube; 2 triangles and 3 rectangles make a triangular prism; 1 square and 4 triangles make a square pyramid.
body_html:
Drawings of solids

A solid takes up space. On paper we draw it flat. Dashed lines show the edges at the back that you cannot see.

A prism or a pyramid is named after its base: a triangular prism has triangle ends, a square pyramid has a square base.

What is a net?

A net is a flat shape that folds up to make a solid. Each part of the net becomes one face. Count the shapes in the net to name the solid.

SolidShapes in the netFacesEdgesVertices
Cube6 equal squares6128
Cuboid6 rectangles (3 matching pairs)6128
Triangular prism2 triangles, 3 rectangles596
Square pyramid1 square, 4 triangles585
Triangular pyramid4 triangles464
Cylinder2 circles, 1 rectangle2 flat faces, 1 curved surface––
Cone1 circle, 1 fan shape1 flat face, 1 curved surface––
Example 1

A net has 1 square and 4 triangles. Which solid does it make?

The square is the base. The 4 triangles fold up and meet at a point.

Answer: a square pyramid

Nets of a cube

A cube has 11 different nets. A pattern of 6 squares is not a net if two squares fold onto the same face.

These are never nets of a cube: 5 squares in a row, a 2-by-2 block of squares, and two squares on the same side of a row of 4.

Squares in a straight line with one square between them become opposite faces.

Example 2

This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?

A, B and C are in a straight line, with B between A and C. So A and C are opposite.

Answer: face C

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking any 6 squares make a cubeFold each square in your head. No row of 5, no 2-by-2 block, no two squares on the same side of a row of 4
Mixing up prisms and pyramidsA prism has 2 matching ends and rectangles; a pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point
Counting only the faces you can seeCount the hidden faces too: a cuboid always has 6 faces
Calling every box a cubeA cube has 6 equal squares; a cuboid has rectangles in matching pairs
Mixing up a cylinder and a coneA cylinder’s net has 2 circles and a rectangle; a cone’s has 1 circle and a fan shape
Swapping edges and verticesEdges are the lines where faces meet; vertices are the corners

faq.q: What do P4 students learn about nets?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students recognise drawings of cubes, cuboids, cones, cylinders, prisms and pyramids, identify the net of a solid, and name the solid that a net folds into.

faq.q: How many nets does a cube have?
faq.a: A cube has 11 different nets. Each one has 6 squares, and no two squares fold onto the same face.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with nets?
faq.a: Thinking that any 6 squares make a cube. A row of 5 squares, a 2-by-2 block, or two squares on the same side of a row of 4 will never fold into a cube.

faq.q: Are nets in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Nets are part of Geometry in the Primary 4 MOE Mathematics Syllabus (2021), and the ideas come back in later work on solids and in the PSLE.

sets.title: Name the solid from its drawing

items.q: What is the name of this solid?
items.e: It has a triangle base and 3 more triangles that meet at a point, so it is a triangular pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this solid?
items.e: It has 2 matching triangles at the ends, joined by rectangles, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: Which solid is shown in this drawing?
items.e: It has 6 rectangular faces, and the faces opposite each other match, so it is a cuboid. It is not a cube, because its faces are not all squares.

items.q: In this drawing of a cuboid, what do the dashed lines show?
c: edges at the back that you cannot see
items.e: A drawing of a solid is flat. Dashed lines show the hidden edges at the back, so you can see the whole shape.
A has 2 matching hexagons at the ends joined by rectangles. The others come to a point, so they are not prisms.
It has 1 flat circular face, 1 curved surface and a point at the top, so it is a cone.

items.q: Which solid is shown in this drawing?
items.e: It has 2 matching hexagons (6 sides) at the ends, joined by rectangles, so it is a hexagonal prism.

items.q: Name this solid.
items.e: It has 6 rectangular faces, and the faces opposite each other match, so it is a cuboid. It is not a cube, because its faces are not all squares.

items.q: Name this solid.
items.e: It has 2 matching pentagons (5 sides) at the ends, joined by rectangles, so it is a pentagonal prism.

items.q: A solid has 1 flat face that is a circle, 1 curved surface and a point at the top. What is the solid?
items.e: It has 1 flat circular face, 1 curved surface and a point at the top, so it is a cone. A pyramid has flat triangles, not a curved surface.
C has 6 rectangular faces. The others are a triangular prism, a square pyramid and a cylinder.
It has 2 flat circular faces and 1 curved surface, so it is a cylinder.

items.q: Name this solid.
items.e: It has 2 matching triangles at the ends, joined by rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. A prism can stand on its end; it is still a prism.
D has a square base and triangles that meet at a point. A prism has 2 matching ends joined by rectangles.

items.q: A solid has 2 flat faces that are circles and 1 curved surface. What is the solid?
items.e: It has 2 flat circular faces and 1 curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A cone has only 1 circle.

items.q: What is the name of this solid?
items.e: All 6 faces are squares of the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: Which solid is shown in this drawing?
items.e: It has 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at a point at the top, so it is a square pyramid. A pyramid is named after the shape of its base.

items.q: What is the name of this solid?
items.e: It has 1 hexagon base (6 sides) and triangles that meet at a point, so it is a hexagonal pyramid. A prism would have 2 hexagons and rectangles.

items.q: The base of a pyramid is a pentagon. What is the name of the pyramid?
items.e: A pyramid is named after its base. A pentagon has 5 sides, so it is a pentagonal pyramid. A prism would have 2 pentagons.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. 3 edges round each triangle end and 3 long edges joining them: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. There are 3 corners on each triangle end: 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: How many edges does a triangular pyramid have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. 3 edges round the base and 3 going up to the top: 3 + 3 = 6.
A cone has 1 flat circular face (the base) and 1 curved surface that comes to a point.

items.q: How many vertices does a hexagonal prism have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles), 18 edges and 12 vertices. 6 corners on each hexagon end: 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: This is a square pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 edges round the base and 4 going up to the top: 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Which solid has 5 faces and 5 vertices?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square, 4 triangles) and 5 vertices (4 on the base, 1 at the top). A triangular prism also has 5 faces, but it has 6 vertices.

items.q: How many vertices does a square pyramid have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 corners on the base and 1 at the top: 4 + 1 = 5.
A cylinder has 2 flat circular faces, one at each end, and 1 curved surface round the side.

items.q: This is a hexagonal pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: 6 edges round the hexagon base and 6 edges going up to the top: 6 + 6 = 12. 7 is the number of vertices (6 + 1).

items.q: Which solid has 9 edges and 6 vertices?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 on each triangle end).

items.q: How many edges does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. There are 4 edges on the top, 4 on the bottom and 4 going up the sides.

items.q: This is a hexagonal pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: The base is 1 hexagon, and there is 1 triangle on each of its 6 sides: 1 + 6 = 7 faces. 8 is the number of faces of a hexagonal prism (2 hexagons and 6 rectangles).

items.q: This is a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. You can see only 3 faces. The bottom, the back and one side are hidden, but they still count.

items.q: This is a square pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Do not forget the square base underneath.

items.q: A cube and a cuboid are compared. Which statement is true?
c: They have the same number of edges
items.e: Both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Only the shapes of the faces are different: a cube has 6 squares.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Vertices are the corners: 4 at the front and 4 at the back.

items.q: This is a triangular pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Do not forget the triangle base underneath.

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons and 5 rectangles), 15 edges and 10 vertices. 2 pentagon ends + 5 rectangles = 7.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Dashed lines show the edges at the back that you cannot see.

sets.title: Which nets fold into a cube?

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: D is not a net of a cube: it has a 2-by-2 block of squares, but only 3 faces of a cube meet at a corner, so two squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cube?
items.e: C folds into a cube with no gaps and no overlaps. Each of the others has two squares that fold onto the same face, so one face is left open.

items.q: How many of these patterns are nets of a cube?
items.e: Fold each one in your head. A, C and D fold into a cube. B does not: it has a 2-by-2 block of squares, but only 3 faces of a cube meet at a corner, so two squares overlap.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?

sets.title: Nets of cuboids, prisms and pyramids

items.q: Which shapes make the net of a triangular prism?
items.e: The 2 triangles are the ends and the 3 rectangles join them. 1 square and 4 triangles is the net of a square pyramid.

items.q: The net of a pyramid has 1 pentagon. How many triangles does it have?
items.e: A pentagon has 5 sides, and there is 1 triangle on each side: 5 triangles. 2 would be the pentagons of a prism.

items.q: In the net of a square pyramid, the square has sides of 6 cm. How long is the bottom edge of each triangle?
items.e: Each triangle is joined to one side of the square, so its bottom edge is as long as that side: 6 cm. 24 cm is the distance all the way round the square.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cuboid?
items.e: A folds into a closed cuboid. The others do not (B: it has only 5 faces, so one face of the cuboid is missing; C: the 4 sides are in the wrong order, so the faces that should be opposite are not the same size; D: one lid is too long, so it does not match the face opposite it).

items.q: A cuboid measures 5 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm. How many faces in its net measure 5 cm by 3 cm?
items.e: The top and the bottom are both 5 cm by 3 cm. Opposite faces of a cuboid are the same, so the faces come in 3 pairs.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cuboid?
items.e: B folds into a closed cuboid. The others do not (A: both lids are on the top edge, so they fold onto the same face and the bottom is left open; C: it has only 5 faces, so one face of the cuboid is missing; D: the 4 sides are in the wrong order, so the faces that should be opposite are not the same size).

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: C has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. Of the others, one makes a square pyramid, one makes a triangular pyramid, and one has only 2 rectangles, so it cannot close up.

items.q: The ends of a triangular prism are triangles with all 3 sides 3 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What size is each rectangle in its net?
items.e: Each rectangle is as wide as one side of the triangle (3 cm) and as long as the prism (10 cm).

items.q: This net is folded into a cuboid. Which face is opposite face T?
items.e: Faces T and U are the two lids: one folds over the top and the other folds under the bottom, so they are opposite. Face P touches face T in the net, so it is next to it, not opposite.

items.q: Which net folds into a square pyramid?
items.e: B has 1 square and 4 triangles, one on each side of the square. One wrong net has only 3 triangles, so one side is left open. The others make a triangular prism and a cuboid.

items.q: This net of a cuboid has one face missing. What shape is the missing face?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces. The net shows 5, so the bottom is missing. It must match the top face, which is a rectangle, because opposite faces of a cuboid are the same.

items.q: Which net folds into a pentagonal prism?
items.e: C has 2 pentagons and 5 rectangles. One wrong net has only 1 pentagon, one has 2 hexagons (a hexagonal prism) and one has 1 pentagon with triangles (a pentagonal pyramid).

items.q: This net of a triangular prism has one face missing. What shape is the missing face?
items.e: A triangular prism has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The net shows 3 rectangles and only 1 triangle, so the missing face is the second triangle (the other end).

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular pyramid?
items.e: D has 4 triangles: 1 base and 3 that fold up to meet at a point. One wrong net has only 3 triangles. The others make a square pyramid and a triangular prism.

items.q: How many rectangles are there in the net of a hexagonal prism?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides, and each side joins a rectangle, so there are 6 rectangles. The net also has 2 hexagons: 8 faces in all.

items.q: This net is folded into a cuboid. Which face is opposite face Q?
items.e: Faces Q and S are the same size and have one face (R) between them in the strip, so they fold onto opposite sides. In a cuboid, opposite faces are always the same size and shape.

items.q: A cube has edges of 4 cm. Which shapes make its net?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, and every face is a square with sides as long as the edges: 4 cm. 8 is the number of vertices, not faces.

items.q: This net of a square pyramid has one face missing. What shape is the missing face?
items.e: A square pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles. The net shows only 3 triangles, so a triangle is missing on the bottom side of the square. The square base is already there.

items.q: How many triangles are there in the net of a square pyramid?
items.e: There is 1 triangle on each side of the square base: 4 triangles. Together with the square, the net has 5 faces.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cuboid?
items.e: D is not a net of a cuboid: one lid is too long, so it does not match the face opposite it. The other three each fold into a closed cuboid.

sets.title: Which solid does the net make? Boxes, hats and tents

items.q: Ryan draws a net with 2 hexagons and 6 rectangles for a gift box. Which solid will the box be?
items.e: 2 matching hexagons joined by rectangles make a prism, so it is a hexagonal prism. A pyramid has only 1 base and triangles.

items.q: Devi makes a dice for a maths game from this net. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 2. So the missing number is 7 − 2 = 5.

items.q: Zhi Hao makes a net of a cube from card. Each square is 10 cm by 10 cm. What is the area of the net?
items.e: Each square has an area of 10 × 10 = 100 cm². There are 6 squares: 6 × 100 = 600 cm². 400 cm² counts only 4 faces.

items.q: Raju cuts out a net of a cube (6 squares in one piece) and folds it. How many edges must he tape to close the cube?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges. The 6 squares of the net are joined by 5 folds, so 12 − 5 = 7 edges are still open and need tape.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which solid does it make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: What solid can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. One is the base and the other 3 meet at a point, so they fold into a triangular pyramid.

items.q: Which solid does this net make?
items.e: There is 1 hexagon (the base) and 6 triangles that meet at a point. They fold into a hexagonal pyramid.

items.q: What solid can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 2 pentagons (the ends) and 5 rectangles joining them. They fold into a pentagonal prism.

items.q: Priya builds a model of a square pyramid with straws and balls of plasticine: one straw for each edge and one ball for each vertex. What does she need?
items.e: A square pyramid has 8 edges (4 round the base and 4 up to the top) and 5 vertices (4 on the base and 1 at the top).

items.q: Ahmad makes a birthday party hat from a fan shape (part of a circle). The hat has no base. What solid shape is the hat?
items.e: The fan shape rolls up into a curved surface that comes to a point, so the hat is a cone without its circle base. A triangle has straight edges, so it cannot roll into a round hat.
There is 1 circle (the base) and a fan shape (part of a circle) that rolls up into a curved surface with a point. They fold into a cone.

items.q: What solid can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a cuboid. The top and bottom are squares, but the 4 sides are thin rectangles, so it is not a cube.

items.q: Mrs Lim’s class makes gift boxes for Children’s Day. Each net has 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. What solid is each box?
items.e: 6 rectangles in matching pairs fold into a cuboid. A cube would need 6 squares, all the same size.

items.q: Which solid does this net make?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles joining them. They fold into a triangular prism. The triangles do not have to have equal sides.

items.q: Which solid does this net make?
items.e: There are 2 circles (the flat ends) and a rectangle that rolls up into the curved surface. They fold into a cylinder.

items.q: Arjun’s Scouts CCA puts up a tent shaped like a triangular prism, with a floor. Each face is one piece of fabric. How many pieces of fabric does the tent have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangles (2 sloping sides and the floor).

items.q: Kavya makes a model cube with straws, one straw for each edge. Each straw is 10 cm long. What is the total length of the straws?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges: 12 × 10 = 120 cm. 60 cm counts the faces (6) and 80 cm counts the vertices (8).

items.q: A drink can is a cylinder. Its paper label goes all the way round the can once, with no overlap. What shape is the label when it is peeled off and laid flat?
items.e: The curved surface of a cylinder unrolls into a rectangle. The 2 circles are the top and bottom of the can.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which solid does it make?
items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at a point. They fold into a square pyramid.

items.q: Which solid does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 squares, all the same size. They fold into a cube.
